summary: PulseGuard v0.6.28 fixes the incomplete-install/preflight failure exposed on a real OneDrive/Desktop installation and adds guarded local runtime self-repair for required configuration, driver-engine files, and working folders.

sections.heading: FIX + OPTIMIZE preflight now self-repairs required folders
sections.detail: Backups, Reports, Logs, Data and DisabledStartup folders are created automatically when missing and then write-tested. A missing empty working folder no longer stops the repair workflow.

sections.heading: Critical runtime/config files have recovery copies
sections.detail: PulseGuard now ships recovery copies of process_rules.json, knowledge_base.json, vendor_update_rules.json, registry_cleanup_rules.json, PulseGuard_DriverEngine.ps1 and PulseGuard_DriverCatalog.json. If one of those primary files is missing, PulseGuard restores only the missing file from its bundled recovery copy and never overwrites an existing primary file through this self-heal path.

sections.heading: Release validation now rejects incomplete packages
sections.detail: The updater now treats every critical rule/config file and its recovery copy as required release payload. A release missing these files is rejected before installation instead of being allowed to create a partially functional PulseGuard installation.

sections.heading: Runtime layout validation is stricter
sections.detail: PulseGuard startup/runtime layout checks now cover the rule/config files and recovery payload needed by FIX + OPTIMIZE, driver scanning and repair preflight, preventing silent partial installs from reaching the repair workflow.

sections.heading: All v0.6.27 diagnostics and repair fixes retained
sections.detail: The SFC corruption repair gate, PCIe WHEA Event 17 resolution, historical WHEA handling, unattended WinGet/restart reporting, protected PATH classification, Deep Clean reporting and driver-update audit changes remain included.
